record.original_question: Characterize all connected signed graphs whose spectral radius does not exceed sqrt(2 + sqrt(5)).

evidence.quote: Problem 3.11 (Hoffman Program for Signed Graphs). Characterize all connected signed graphs whose spectral radius does not exceed p 2 + √ 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair $\dot{G}=(G,\sigma)$, where $G=(V,E)$ is a finite simple undirected graph and $\sigma\colon E\to\{+1,-1\}$ is a sign function on its edges. The adjacency matrix of $\dot{G}$ is the symmetric $|V|\times|V|$ matrix $A(\dot{G})$ whose $(u,v)$-entry equals $\sigma(uv)$ if $uv\in E$ and $0$ otherwise. The spectral radius $\rho(\dot{G})$ of $\dot{G}$ is the largest absolute value among the eigenvalues of $A(\dot{G})$. The signed graph $\dot{G}$ is connected if its underlying graph $G$ is connected.

Give a complete characterization (up to switching equivalence) of all connected signed graphs $\dot{G}$ satisfying
$$\rho(\dot{G}) \le \sqrt{2+\sqrt{5}}.$$
artifact.category_tag: spectral graph theory of signed graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A 2022 preprint (arXiv:2203.01530), later published in Discrete Mathematics (2023), identifies all signed graphs whose spectral radius does not exceed √(2+√5), providing the characterization sought by the Hoffman program for signed graphs. Subsequent surveys on the Hoffman program report this case as resolved.
